w-jp-003.title: Curry Bread (Karee Pan)

instructions.1: Combine the yeast, milk, and sugar in a small bowl, cover, and set aside for 10 minutes, then stir in the egg.
instructions.2: Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Make a well in the center of the flour and add the liquid mixture, stirring to form a soft dough.
instructions.4: Transfer the dough to an electric mixer fitted with a dough hook and knead for about 5 minutes or until smooth and elastic.
instructions.5: With the mixer motor running, add the chopped butter and mix until the butter is combined and a smooth and silky dough forms.
instructions.6: Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and set aside in a warm place to prove for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
instructions.8: Finely chop the carrot, onion, and garlic.
instructions.9: Peel and cut the potato into bite-sized pieces and cook until soft to make mashed potato. Set aside.
instructions.10: Heat olive oil in a frying pan and cook the onion, carrot, and garlic until soft, then add the beef mince and cook.
instructions.11: Add water to the frying pan and bring it to a boil.
instructions.12: Turn the heat down to low and add the Japanese curry roux. Stir and mix until the roux is dissolved.
instructions.13: Add the mashed potato and simmer until the mixture has thickened.
instructions.14: Pour the mixture into a flat container, and when it is set, divide it into 8 even sizes.
instructions.15: Divide the bread dough into 8 equal-sized balls and knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth.
instructions.16: Wrap a piece of the curry filling with a bread roll.
instructions.17: Spray it with olive oil and roll in panko crumbs to coat the bread. Repeat the process for the other 7 pieces.
instructions.18: Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, cover with a clean damp cloth, and set aside for about 45 minutes or until doubled in size.
instructions.19: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and bake for 15 minutes.

w-jp-003.culturalNotes: Curry Bread (Karee Pan) is a popular Japanese pastry, often enjoyed as a snack or part of a breakfast meal.

w-jp-012.title: Imagawayaki (Obanyaki)

w-jp-012-i1.name: eggs
w-jp-012-i1.standardAmount: 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs well, then add the sugar, honey, and milk and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the flour and baking powder and mix until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
instructions.4: Heat the imagawayaki pan over medium heat and grease it with the neutral oil.
instructions.5: Fill each hole in the pan with about 2 tablespoons of batter, then place a small spoonful of sweet red bean paste in the center of each hole.
instructions.6: Cover the filling with batter, then cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown on the bottom.
instructions.7: Flip the imagawayaki and cook for another 3-4 minutes until golden brown on the other side.
instructions.8: Serve the imagawayaki hot or warm.

w-jp-012.culturalNotes: Imagawayaki is a traditional Japanese sweet often served at festivals and special occasions.

w-jp-013.title: Japanese Milk Bread (Shokupan)

w-jp-013-i1.name: bread flour
w-jp-013-i1.standardAmount: 250g + 20g for the yukone and extra for dusting

instructions.1: In a small saucepan, whisk together 20g bread flour with 100ml water until smooth. Put over a low-medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until a thick paste. This happens fast, around 5 mins. Remove from heat and set aside to cool to room temperature.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, or the bowl of a stand mixer, combine 250g bread flour with the yeast, sugar, and salt. Keep the yeast and salt on opposite sides of the bowl so the salt doesn't touch the yeast directly.
instructions.3: Add the cooled yukone, warm milk, and beaten egg. Mix (by hand or with a dough hook) for about 2 mins until it comes together into a rough dough.
instructions.4: Knead the dough until smooth and elastic, around 8 mins in the mixer. Add the softened butter a little at a time and continue kneading for another 8-10 mins until the dough is soft, glossy, and you can stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing.
instructions.5: Shape the dough into a ball, put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp towel, and leave in a warm place to rise until doubled in size, around 1 hr 30 mins.
instructions.6: Punch down the dough and divide into three equal pieces. Roll each piece on a lightly floured surface into an oval, fold the sides in, then roll up from the bottom into a tight cylinder. Put all three pieces seam-side down side by side into an oiled shokupan or 900g loaf tin.
instructions.7: Cover the tin loosely and leave in a warm place until the dough rises to about 80-90 per cent of the tin's height, around 1 hr. If using a lidded shokupan tin, close the lid once it's close to full.
instructions.8: Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. If not using a lidded tin, brush the top of the loaf with the milk or melted butter. Bake for about 20 mins until deep golden brown, then drop the heat to 170C/150C fan/gas 3 and bake for another 5-10 mins until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the base. Turn the loaf out of the tin immediately and cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing. Will keep wrapped for up to three days.

w-jp-013.culturalNotes: Japanese milk bread (shokupan) is a soft, fluffy bread known for its silky texture. It is characterized by its mild sweetness and smooth texture, making it perfect for breakfast or light snacks.

w-jp-014.title: Japanese Glass Noodle Soup

w-jp-014-i1.name: Eggs
w-jp-014-i1.standardAmount: 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

w-jp-014-i8.name: Soy Sauce
w-jp-014-i8.standardAmount: 1½ Tbsp (use gluten-free soy sauce for GF)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Beat 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell) in a measuring cup or in a bowl with a spout.
instructions.3: Cut the white part of 2 green onions/scallions into thin round pieces. Then, thinly slice the green part diagonally. Set them aside separately.
instructions.4: Cut 3.5 oz medium-firm tofu (momen dofu) into ½-inch (1.3 cm) cubes.
instructions.5: Add 2 Tbsp dried wakame seaweed to a small bowl of water and rehydrate for 5 minutes. Then, drain and squeeze the water out. Set aside.
instructions.6: Preheat a medium pot over medium heat. When the pot is hot, add 2 tsp roasted sesame oil, then the white part of the green onions.
instructions.7: Stir-fry for 30 seconds until the green onions are well coated with the oil. Then, add 2 cups chicken stock/broth and 2 cups water.
instructions.8: Add 1½ Tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt, and ¼ tsp white pepper powder.
instructions.9: After mixing the soup well, cover the pot with a lid and bring it to a boil.
instructions.10: Once boiling, add the tofu and 1 oz dried glass/cellophane noodles (harusame).
instructions.11: Cook the glass noodles according to the package instructions. Stir the noodles in the beginning so they don’t stick to each other or the bottom of the pot.
instructions.12: After the noodles are cooked, adjust the heat so the soup is simmering (a very gentle boil). Slowly pour a steady trickle of the beaten eggs into the soup in a circular motion, starting from the center and spiraling outward. (Don’t pour on top of any egg that you’ve already added to the soup.) Place cooking chopsticks at the edge of the bowl/measuring cup while pouring so the egg will drizzle down the chopsticks in a thin stream. Let the eggs sit without stirring for 20–25 seconds until they’re fluffy and just cooked.
instructions.13: Add the rehydrated wakame seaweed, green parts of the green onions, and 2 tsp toasted white sesame seeds. Remove the saucepan from the heat to prevent overcooking.
instructions.14: Transfer the glass noodles to individual bowls with a pair of tongs. Then pour the soup and other ingredients over the noodles. Serve hot.

w-jp-014.culturalNotes: Japanese Glass Noodle Soup is a popular dish in Japan, often served as a light meal or part of a lunch.

w-jp-015.title: Kamaboko with Salmon Roe

instructions.1: Remove the kamaboko from the refrigerator and let it thaw if frozen.
instructions.2: Wash the shiso leaves and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.3: Place the kamaboko on a serving plate.
instructions.4: Sprinkle the chopped shiso leaves over the surface of the kamaboko.
instructions.5: Add the salmon roe on top of the shiso leaves.

w-jp-015.culturalNotes: Kamaboko is a traditional Japanese fish cake, often served as an appetizer on special occasions.

w-jp-035.title: Tamago Kake Gohan

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. For the steamed rice, ¾ cup (150 g) of uncooked Japanese short-grain rice yields 2¼ US cups (330 g) of cooked white rice.
instructions.2: Add 1 serving of cooked Japanese short-grain rice to a rice bowl. The rice should be steaming hot.
instructions.3: Make a well in the middle of the rice. Crack 1 large egg (50 g without shell) into the well.
instructions.4: Drizzle a small amount of soy sauce onto the egg.
instructions.5: Add toppings of your choice. I like to sprinkle katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes) around the egg in the rice.
instructions.6: Drizzle a bit more soy sauce on the toppings if you wish.
instructions.7: Stir the ingredients with a pair of chopsticks until the egg is fully incorporated into the rice and turns a pale yellow color.

w-jp-035.culturalNotes: Tamago Kake Gohan is a traditional Japanese breakfast dish often served in the morning. It is known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-jp-036.title: Tamagoyaki

instructions.1: Crack the eggs into a medium-sized mixing bowl.
instructions.2: Add the seasonings (shirodashi and water for dashimaki or sugar, salt, and water for atsumaki) and mix them together gently to avoid too much bubble formation.
instructions.3: Strain the egg mixture through a sieve a few times.
instructions.4: Pour about 2 tbsp of oil into a small bowl and soak kitchen paper and set aside.
instructions.5: Heat 2 tsp of olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat until you can feel the heat when you hover your hand over the pan.
instructions.6: Pour 1/3 of the egg mixture into the pan (you should hear a sizzling sound).
instructions.7: Break any bubbles that have formed with the edge of the chopsticks and scramble gently.
instructions.8: When the surface is solidified a little, fold and push the egg to one end of the pan with chopsticks.
instructions.9: Wipe the empty side of the pan with oil-soaked kitchen paper and pour another 1/3 of the egg mixture into the empty space of the pan.
instructions.10: Lift the folded egg up to let the egg mixture run under it.
instructions.11: Fold and roll the egg from one side of the pan and wipe the empty space of the pan with the oil-soaked kitchen paper.
instructions.12: Pour the last 1/3 of the egg mixture and repeat fold and roll.
instructions.13: Turn the heat off and wrap the rolled egg with a thin kitchen towel.
instructions.14: Roll the wrapped egg roll with a sushi mat to shape and rest to cool down.
instructions.15: Once it is cooled down, slice it 2 cm (0.79 inch) thick and serve.

w-jp-036.culturalNotes: Tamagoyaki is a type of Japanese rolled omelette often served in daily meals.

w-jp-037.title: Tuna Tataki

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Grate the ginger and collect 1 tsp ginger (grated, with juice). Slice 1 green onion/scallion thinly and set aside.
instructions.3: Combine the sauce ingredients in a small bowl: the green onions, the grated ginger, 3 Tbsp ponzu, 2 tsp roasted sesame oil, 1 tsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp toasted white sesame seeds. Set aside.
instructions.4: Heat a nonstick frying pan. When the pan is hot, add 2 Tbsp neutral oil. When the oil is hot, add 225 g sashimi-grade yellowfin/ahi tuna and sear it 30 seconds on each side.
instructions.5: When all sides are seared, remove from the heat and let it cool. Slice the tuna into ¼-inch (6-mm) pieces. Pour the sauce on the Tuna Tataki and serve with ½ lemon and Korean chili thread.

w-jp-037.culturalNotes: Tuna Tataki is a traditional Japanese dish often served as a starter or light main course. It is known for its strong and delicious flavor.

w-jp-038.title: Japanese Kakiage Tempura

instructions.1: Cut the onion, carrot, and sweet potato into small pieces.
instructions.2: Wash the shiso leaves and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.3: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the water gradually and mix until you get a thick batter.
instructions.5: Add the vegetables and shiso leaves to the batter and mix well.
instructions.6: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 170 degrees Celsius.
instructions.7: Add a tablespoon of the batter mixture to the hot oil and fry until golden brown.
instructions.8: Remove the kakiage from the oil and place it on a paper towel to drain excess oil.
instructions.9: Repeat the process until all the mixture is used up.

w-jp-038.culturalNotes: Kakiage is a type of Japanese tempura, consisting of small vegetable pieces fried in a batter.

w-ma-029.title: Kebab Maghdour

w-ma-029-i15.name: Eggs
w-ma-029-i15.standardAmount: 3-6 (counting half to a whole egg per person)

w-ma-029-i17.name: Chopped flat leaf parsley or coriander

instructions.1: Prepare the meat by cutting it into 1-inch cubes.
instructions.2: In a bowl, mix the meat with grated onion, garlic, ginger, pepper, parsley and coriander, and vegetable oil. Let the mixture marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: In a pot, add the vegetable and olive oil, then add the finely chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
instructions.4: Add the marinated meat to the pot and sauté for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Add water to cover the meat, then add ginger, salt, cinnamon stick, and ground sweet paprika. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
instructions.6: Add the eggs to the pot and cook for 10 minutes until they are done.
instructions.7: Serve the Kebab Maghdour hot, garnished with chopped parsley.

w-ma-029.culturalNotes: Kebab Maghdour is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions. It is known for its rich spice flavors and tender meat.

w-mx-005.title: Mexican Barbacoa

instructions.1: In a large pot, place the onion, tomatillos, tomatoes, garlic, New Mexico chiles, and ancho chiles. Add 1 cup of water and bring the ingredients to a boil over medium heat.
instructions.2: Gently stir the ingredients and let them boil for 15 minutes until they become soft.
instructions.3: Add the lamb leg, agave nectar, and salt. Add 1/2 cup of water and let the lamb cook on low heat for 4 hours until it becomes tender and easy to shred.
instructions.4: In a small bowl, mix the Chile Colorado Sauce.
instructions.5: Warm the tortillas over medium heat until they become soft.
instructions.6: Serve the barbacoa with tortillas, sliced jicama, cubed avocados, Chile Colorado Sauce, chopped fresh cilantro, and lime wedges.

w-mx-005.culturalNotes: Barbacoa is a traditional Mexican dish typically made from lamb or beef and slow-cooked over low heat.

w-mx-006.title: Bolillo (Mexican Bread Rolls)

instructions.1: Prepare the yeast. In a cup or bowl, heat the water in the microwave or on the stove until it's warm (about 110-115°F). Add the yeast and sugar and mix. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let it stand for 5 minutes until it becomes foamy. If it doesn't become foamy, discard it and start again with a new packet of yeast.
instructions.2: Prepare the dough. In the bowl of a stand mixer (or a large bowl), whisk together the all-purpose flour and salt. Attach the dough hook to the mixer and add the oil and yeast mixture. Mix on medium-low speed for 6-8 minutes (or mix by hand) until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. If the dough is still fairly sticky, knead in 1 tablespoon of additional flour at a time until smooth and elastic. If it's too dry, add 1 tablespoon of additional water at a time.
instructions.3: Rise. Coat a large bowl with oil and transfer the dough to the bowl, shaping it into a ball. Cover it with a kitchen towel and let it rise until it has doubled in size, about 1-1.5 hours.
instructions.4: Shape and rise again. Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces and shape into 7-inch long ovals with a tapered end. Place 3 bolillos on each of the prepared baking sheets and lightly brush the tops with a little oil or spray with cooking spray to keep them moist. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them rise again for 45 minutes.
instructions.5: Preheat the oven. 15 minutes before they’re finished resting, fill a 9x13-inch baking dish with 10 cups of water and place it on the lowest rack in the oven to create a moist environment. Preheat the oven to 425°F.
instructions.6: Cut the bolillos. Make a ¼-inch deep cut lengthwise down the middle of each bolillo using a very sharp knife.
instructions.7: Bake. Spray the tops of the bolillos with a little water, then transfer them to the oven and bake for 30-35 minutes, until golden brown.
instructions.8: Let them cool for at least 10 minutes before serving.

w-mx-006.culturalNotes: Bolillo is a traditional Mexican bread used in many dishes such as tacos and sandwiches.

w-mx-021.title: Clemole de Pollo

instructions.1: Break open the chiles and remove the seeds and veins.
instructions.2: Place the chiles in a pan and cover with water.
instructions.3: Bring the water to a boil and then turn off the heat and let the chiles reconstitute for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the whole tomatoes to a pot and cover them with water.
instructions.5: Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
instructions.6: Blend the tomatoes and chiles with a little bit of the water you used to soak the chiles to form a loose paste.
instructions.7: Set aside the chile tomato base.
instructions.8: Put the chicken in the pot with 8 cups of water, the whole onion, and the head of garlic. Cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
instructions.9: Add the chunks of corn, chayote, and epazote. Cook for 15 more minutes over low heat.
instructions.10: Add the chunks of zucchini squash and green beans.
instructions.11: Strain the blended guajillo chile tomato base directly into the pot.
instructions.12: Bring to a boil and remove any foam that rises to the top.
instructions.13: Reduce the heat and cook for 20 minutes.
instructions.14: Add 1 tsp of salt. Then add as much salt as needed to your taste.
instructions.15: Discard the onion, epazote, and head of garlic before serving.

w-mx-021.culturalNotes: Clemole de Pollo is a traditional Mexican dish served on special occasions.

w-mx-022.title: Cocada (Dulce)

instructions.1: In a large pot over medium heat, cook water, sugar, and cloves. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Heat until the mixture reaches the soft-ball stage on a candy thermometer (about 240F).
instructions.2: Using a spoon, carefully discard the cloves.
instructions.3: Add shredded coconut and milk. The mixture will clump. Continue to stir until smooth. Simmer for a few minutes.
instructions.4: Spoon into serving dishes and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

w-mx-022.culturalNotes: Cocada is a traditional Mexican dessert, typically made from coconut and sugar.

w-mx-036.title: Mole de Olla

w-mx-036-i15.name: carrot
w-mx-036-i15.standardAmount: 3 small or 1 large (cut into large pieces)

instructions.1: Rinse the meat and pat dry thoroughly with a paper towel. In a large stockpot, place the meat, onion, garlic, and bay leaves. Cover with 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce heat to simmer gently. Use a slotted spoon to remove any foam that rises to the surface. The meat will take about 1 ½ to 2 hours to cook.
instructions.2: While the meat is cooking, prepare the sauce. Fill a small pot with 2 cups of hot water and set aside. I like roasting the ingredients of the salsa since it gives a rustic flavor to the soup. Now, slightly roast the peppers in a hot griddle, turning once. Remember, this step takes only a few seconds if you leave the peppers longer on the hot griddle they will have a bitter taste. Place the roasted peppers in the pot with the hot water to soften them, at least 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Roast the tomato, garlic, and onion on the hot griddle. The garlic will take less time to roast, so remove promptly. Remove its peel and place in your blender pitcher. Once the tomato and onion are roasted, place them into the blender as well. Once the peppers have softened, add them into the blender along with a cup of the soaking water. Proceed to puree until you have a very smooth sauce. Set aside.
instructions.4: To cook the vegetables: In another medium size saucepan, add 3 cups of water and the pieces of corn to cook over medium-high heat. 8-10 minutes later, add the xoconostle, chayote, and carrots. About 3 minutes after that, add the potatoes (if using) and finally the squash and green beans to cook for 4 more minutes. Don’t worry if they still look uncooked after this time, they will finish cooking with the meat and sauce.
instructions.5: Check your meat. If it is already cooked and tender, remove the garlic, onion, and bay leaf. Now, add the sauce and the Epazote sprigs, stir, and keep simmering for about 8 more minutes. Add the vegetables and stir well. Let it simmer for another 6 minutes to allow all the flavors to blend. You can pour it using a strainer if you want, personally, I don’t use a strainer with this soup since I like how the sauce gives the soup a thicker texture.
instructions.6: To serve, ladle the soup in large bowls with some portions of meat, corn, carrots, chayote, xoconostle, squash, potato, and green beans. Garnish with chopped onion, cilantro, epazote, and lime juice.
instructions.7: Serve with some warm corn tortillas. There you have it, a whole meal in a bowl!

w-mx-036.culturalNotes: Mole de Olla is a traditional Mexican soup rich in flavors, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-mx-040.title: Orejas (Palmiers) - A Sweet Bread

instructions.1: In a bowl, stir together sugar and cinnamon.
instructions.2: Place one sheet of puff pastry on the counter (no flour needed). Lightly roll to flatten.
instructions.3: Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon mixture evenly over the pastry. Gently roll over to press the sugar into the dough.
instructions.4: Fold 1 inch from each side toward the center. Repeat folding until both sides meet in the middle.
instructions.5: Cut the folded pastry into ¾-inch slices. Dip in extra cinnamon sugar if desired.
instructions.6: Repeat with the second sheet of pastry.
instructions.7: Bake at 375°F for 20 minutes. Flip each piece and bake 4-5 more minutes until crisp and golden.
instructions.8: Let cool before serving or storing.

w-mx-040.culturalNotes: Orejas (Palmiers) are a popular French pastry, but they are also known in Mexico as a type of sweet bread.

w-mx-046.title: Chile Relleno

w-mx-046-i2.name: Monterey Jack cheese
w-mx-046-i2.standardAmount: 8 ounces (cut into long strips or shredded)

instructions.1: Roast the poblano peppers over medium heat until the skin is blackened. Place them in a sealed plastic bag for 10 minutes to cool.
instructions.2: Peel the peppers and cut off the stem. Gently open the peppers and remove the seeds and inner membrane.
instructions.3: Stuff the peppers with Monterey Jack cheese. Set the stuffed peppers aside.
instructions.4: In a bowl, beat the eggs with salt. In another bowl, place the flour.
instructions.5: Dip the stuffed peppers in the flour, then in the beaten eggs.
instructions.6: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Fry the peppers until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.7: Make the tomato sauce by blending the tomatoes, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, salt, and olive oil in a blender until smooth.
instructions.8: Serve the stuffed peppers with the tomato sauce on the side.

w-mx-046.culturalNotes: Chile relleno is a traditional Mexican dish often served on special occasions.

w-mx-048.title: Mexican Cinnamon Tea

instructions.1: Place the water and cinnamon in a medium-sized saucepan and bring to a boil.
instructions.2: Let it boil for 3-5 minutes, then remove from heat.
instructions.3: Let it steep for an additional 30 minutes or to taste based on desired strength.
instructions.4: Add honey to taste.

w-mx-048.culturalNotes: Mexican cinnamon tea is a traditional drink that is very popular in Mexico, especially during holidays and special occasions.

w-mx-049.title: Fish Fillet with Garlic Sauce

w-mx-049-i4.name: Vegetable oil (or a mix of half olive oil and half vegetable oil)

instructions.1: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Set aside while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over low heat. Once hot, fry the garlic slices until they are golden. Make sure to remove them promptly once they are lightly golden; if you leave them longer, they will get a bitter taste.
instructions.3: If using the flour, dust the fillets with the flour lightly. Then, turn the heat to medium-high on the frying pan where you cooked the garlic. Once hot, add the fish and cook on both sides. The cooking time will depend on the fish’s thickness. It will be about 2-3 minutes per side for those fillets about 1/3 inch thick, and about 5-7 minutes for thicker fillets.
instructions.4: Remove the fish from the frying pan and place it on a cooling rack with paper towel underneath to absorb any excess fat.
instructions.5: Serve the fish garnished with the chopped parsley and golden garlic slices. (And if you add a little dab of butter, oh heavens!)

w-mx-049.culturalNotes: This dish is one of the popular dishes in Mexican cuisine, often served as a main course at family gatherings.

w-mx-050.title: Green Chile and Cheese Quesadilla

instructions.1: Preheat a comal for 1 minute over medium-low heat.
instructions.2: Warm tortillas for 1 minute on one side, flip and sprinkle some of the cheese on one of the tortillas, add chile, and top with another tortilla and press gently with a spatula.
instructions.3: Flip occasionally until quesadillas are golden brown on each side and cheese has melted.
instructions.4: Repeat with remaining tortillas and ingredients.
instructions.5: Top them with salsa and guacamole, if desired.

w-mx-050.culturalNotes: Quesadilla is a popular dish in Mexico, served as a snack or main meal.
